TOKYO, Oct 27 : Moody's sees encouraging signs in Japan's return to sustained growth and stable inflation, but a key test will be whether that resilience can withstand future shocks, the rating agency's Japan sovereign analyst told Reuters on Tuesday. Moody's rates Japan at A1, its fifth-highest investment-grade rating, with a stable outlook, unchanged since its 2014 downgrade of Japan from Aa3. "We're starting to see what looks more like sustained growth and inflation expectations that are reasonably well anchored around 2 per cent," said Martin Petch, a vice president at the sovereign risk group of Moody's Ratings. "That's been something that's changed," Petch said in an interview, referring to a shift from decades of weak growth and chronically low inflation.

Petch declined to speculate on future rating actions, but said Moody's was watching to see if recent changes in Japan's economic and inflation environment prove sustainable, along with reforms that boost productivity and tackle demographic woes. A key test, he added, is whether Japan can maintain growth and inflation stability through future economic shocks. "You can generally tell when growth has become sustained when the economy has dealt with a shock," Petch said, pointing out that Japan had coped well with recent energy-price shocks while the central bank keeps up efforts to normalise policy. LITTLE IMMEDIATE THREAT SEEN TO CREDIT PROFILE Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's food sales tax cut and ambitious spending plans rattled bond markets this year, but Petch suggested the measures have posed little immediate threat to Japan's credit profile. Their fiscal impact would depend on whether the government delivered on its pledge to offset the resulting revenue loss, he added. Although ministries have sought a record 143 trillion yen ($908 billion) in initial spending requests, Petch said the rise was relatively modest compared with combined initial and supplementary budgets. This reinforced Moody's view that there has been no meaningful departure from Japan's recent consolidation trend, he added. But uncertainties hover over the government's 370-trillion-yen public-private investment initiative, Petch said. These include the extent to which the private sector joins the initiative, and whether it can bring the productivity gains needed to offset Japan's demographic headwinds, he added. ($1=157.4700 yen)

Source: Reuters

Oct 27 : Leading men's doubles players have called on the ATP Tour to reconsider plans that would reduce the size of the doubles competitions at events and move prize money to the singles format. In a letter addressed to the ATP board and management and signed by 137 active players, 33 former players and 20 federations, the group said it understood the need for reforms but was deeply concerned about the plans being discussed. The ATP said this month it was reviewing potential changes to the size of the doubles draws at tournaments as part of its plans for 2028 and beyond, with the freed-up funds going towards singles qualifying and early-round prize money. "The current plans would shift about $20 million in prize money from doubles to singles, while cutting a significant number of professional opportunities for doubles specialists," the group wrote.

"That shift would make it much harder for talented players to build and sustain a doubles career. A healthy professional sport cannot rely solely on a small group of top stars; it needs pathways for players to develop, compete and earn a living." Reuters has contacted the ATP for comment. The governing body of men's tennis said earlier this month doubles will continue to be a core part of the tour and its reviews were focused on identifying a model for its sustainable long-term future. It added that discussions would continue with the Player Advisory Council. The ATP is set to hold its year-end meetings in Turin next month. The plans being discussed include cutting the number of doubles teams at elite ATP Masters 1000 events to 16 from 32, with events below that level featuring smaller fields. Apart from the Grand Slams and Olympic Games, doubles receives much less attention than singles and few top singles players commit to playing the format, though it is hugely popular at club level. Dutch player Sem Verbeek said the ATP should look after the interests of all its members. "Tennis is more than a business," the doubles world number 60 said on X. "It's a legacy built on joy, health and sportsmanship. A sport built on those values should open doors, not close them." The ATP outlined plans this month to boost its bonus pool to $50 million from $21.5 million, and reshape its rankings and calendar as part of a package aimed at lifting player compensation to $350 million from 2028.

Source: Reuters

Oct 27 : Having run the rule over more than 50 players during the tour of South Africa, New Zealand coach Dave Rennie will finally get a look at Leicester Fainga'anuku on the season-ending trip to Britain. Fainga'anuku was named among six loose forwards in the All Blacks' squad for next month's Nations Championship tests against Scotland, Wales and England, though there is every chance the explosive 27-year-old could be deployed on the wing or in the midfield as the occasion demands. Fainga'anuku missed the first tranche of Nations Championship matches in July and the subsequent four-test tour of South Africa after sustaining a fractured fibula and high ankle sprain playing for the Canterbury Crusaders in Super Rugby Pacific. More recently, his provincial campaign for Tasman wrapped up early with a head-knock and concussion in the final rounds, and he may not be fully fit for the opening test against Scotland in Edinburgh on November 7.

Rennie, however, is confident Fainga'anuku can make a difference when his time comes. “It’s less (playing time) than we would have liked,” Rennie told New Zealand media on Tuesday of Fainga'anuku's disrupted buildup. “Still, it’s better to have him in the group for the next four or five weeks. He’s in reasonable nick now.” Having once starred on the wing for the Crusaders, Fainga'anuku made a successful switch to the back row this season. With All Blacks captain Ardie Savea sidelined, along with season-ending injuries to Luke Jacobson and Shannon Frizell, Fainga'anuku takes his place ahead of test loose forward Du’Plessis Kirifi and impressive young flanker Semisi Ta'eiloa. "It gives you massive flexibility," Rennie said of Fainga'anuku's versatility. "You can name a 5-3 bench but it’s generally a 6-2 (split) and he can definitely make (an) impact in all of those spots." Rennie will also have a first look at number eight Christian Lio-Willie, who debuted last year and played three tests under former head coach Scott Robertson.   He said there were serious discussions about taking Lio-Willie to South Africa before they opted for other players ahead of him. "He's really tough. He's got a big engine, a really high skill-set and suits the type of game we're trying to play. We’re really excited for him," he said. Still coming back from a calf injury, Richie Mo'unga was included in the tour squad with incumbent flyhalf Damian McKenzie and the uncapped Josh Jacomb. Mo'unga had recovered quicker than hoped from his injury but the elite playmaker is more likely to play in the second test against Wales, rather than come straight back in for Scotland, Rennie said.

Source: Reuters

Jay-Z will headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show in February, the National Football League announced on Monday (Oct 26). The show at the NFL championship game is the most-coveted showcase in the world of music. US television ratings for the halftime performance often top 100 million viewers and rank higher than the audience for the game itself.  Iconic artistes including the Rolling Stones, Beyonce, Madonna, Prince and Bruce Springsteen have taken the Super Bowl stage over the years. Puerto Rican rapper Bad Bunny headlined the show at the last Super Bowl. Next year's Super Bowl will take place on Feb 14 in Los Angeles. It will be broadcast on Walt Disney's ABC and ESPN television networks and will stream on Disney+ and the ESPN app.

Jay-Z poses during the Met Gala, an annual fundraising gala held for the benefit of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's Costume Institute, on May 4, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Daniel Cole)

Jay-Z's company, Roc Nation, has produced the Super Bowl halftime show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer. "For several years, we've had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I've seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show," NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him." Jay-Z is known for hits such as 99 Problems and Hard Knock Life. The 56-year-old rapper has also collaborated with artists including Alicia Keys on Empire State of Mind and his wife, Beyonce, on Crazy in Love.

Source: Reuters/hq

SEOUL, Oct 27 : South Korea's semiconductor exports could fall by $50 billion to $100 billion compared with earlier forecasts if capital spending on artificial intelligence by major US technology firms slows next year, according to central bank data. In a written response submitted to lawmaker Ahn Do-geol, the Bank of Korea (BOK) modelled a "pessimistic scenario" to assess the economic fallout if US tech giants curb their aggressive infrastructure outlays. Under the scenario, a sudden export shortfall would shave approximately 0.4 per centage point off South Korea's gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate next year, by driving the country's current account surplus well below the central bank's initial projection of $430 billion for 2027. The scenario assumed a 10 per cent decline in Korean semiconductor unit prices.

The report said combined capital expenditure by five major US technology firms, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle, has been growing rapidly, from $40 billion last year to an estimated $80 billion this year, and is projected to reach $110 billion next year. However, the BOK cautioned that considerable uncertainty remains over the trajectory of AI demand and the broader memory chip business cycle.

SEOUL, Oct 27 : South Korean pop music agency JYP Entertainment's shares jumped 10 per cent on Tuesday after Korean media reported Japan's Nexroc Group and related firm SVCV Inc were planning to announce a tender offer to buy up to a 50 per cent stake in the company. The 50 per cent stake is worth about 700 billion won ($528.04 million) based on JYP's current market capitalisation. JYP said it has not received a tender offer. Nexroc Group was not immediately available to comment. JYP Entertainment, founded by South Korean singer-songwriter and producer Park Jin-young (J.Y. Park), is one of South Korea’s leading K-pop entertainment companies, with its main artists including popular K-pop groups such as TWICE, Stray Kids, ITZY and DAY6.

FAST

SEOUL: South Korea's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter as a global AI chip boom boosted exports and investments, advance central bank estimates showed on Tuesday (Oct 27), though domestic demand remained weak. Gross domestic product expanded 1.0 per cent in the July-September quarter from the preceding three months, when it grew 0.6 per cent. It was stronger than a median 0.7 per cent increase tipped in a Reuters poll of economists. It was also higher than the Bank of Korea's forecast of 0.3 per cent in August, when the central bank projected this year's growth at 3.3 per cent. The economy is now seen growing 3.7 per cent this year, if GDP in the fourth quarter stays at the same level as the third quarter. "It is estimated that about half of economic growth is being driven by semiconductors," Lee Dong-won, director general of the Bank of Korea's economic statistics department, told a briefing.

Exports and investments are expected to remain robust in the fourth quarter, Lee said, adding that chip production volume will expand further next year while prices will continue to grow but at a slower pace. Private consumption, which fell for the first time in nearly four years in the third quarter, will likely recover gradually, as dividend payouts by chip firms to their shareholders in the fourth quarter and bonus payments to employees in the first quarter of 2027 boost household income, Lee said. Amid the global boom in AI investment, South Korea's exports topped US$800 billion in January to September, higher than last year's full-year record, and are on track to exceed US$1 trillion this year, which will make South Korea the fourth country to reach the milestone, after the US, China and Germany. The Bank of Korea kept interest rates unchanged last week, after back-to-back hikes in July and September, but maintained a hawkish stance by upgrading its economic growth forecasts and remaining upbeat about the country's export momentum. "Exports and investments are leading growth, but the downside is that private consumption remains weak compared with the overall growth momentum," said Park Sang-hyun, an economist at iM Securities. "There could be short-term boosts, but it is difficult to expect strong momentum given labour market conditions and restrictive interest rates," Park said. In a separate central bank survey released on Thursday, consumer sentiment fell slightly in October, as the outlook for household income and consumer spending weakened. In the third quarter, exports rose 2.3 per cent on demand for semiconductors, machinery and electric equipment, while imports grew 2.4 per cent. Facilities investment jumped 4.1 per cent, led by machinery such as semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Private consumption fell 0.2 per cent as financial services declined on a stock market slump and car purchases fell due to strikes at major automakers. On a year-on-year basis, GDP grew 3.4 per cent, after rising 3.7 per cent in the quarter before, also stronger than economists' expectations for a 3.0 per cent increase.

Source: Reuters/dy/ec

Oct 27 : Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war on Iran kept supply fears at bay, but Brent stayed close to six-month highs as attacks on Saudi Arabia lowered hopes of immediate stability in the region. Brent crude futures were down 66 cents, or 0.57 per cent, at $115.15 a barrel as of 0000 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 44 cents, or 0.43 per cent, at $101.32. Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia said the visit sought to establish open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation". The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media reported. Hopes of resolution in the conflict erased some fears of supply disruption, lowering risks and pressuring oil prices.

October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017. The war has rippled across the Middle East, placing the Strait of Hormuz at the center of the turmoil. The narrow waterway carried around a fifth of the world's energy supplies before the conflict erupted in February. Last week, Brent prices surged to more than $117 a barrel, the highest level since April, after a wave of Iranian attacks on tankers around the strait. Brent prices touched $117 on Monday as well. Elsewhere, Russian refiners are raising diesel production in October after the government granted export quotas following the Kremlin's supply agreement with the US, two industry sources close to the matter said.

TOKYO, Oct 27 : A key gauge of Japan's service-sector inflation rose 3.7 per cent in September from a year earlier, data showed on Tuesday, a sign of mounting price pressures that will likely keep the central bank on track for further interest rate hikes. • The year-on-year rise in the services producer price index, which tracks the prices that companies charge each other for services, followed a revised 3.5 per cent gain in August, data from the Bank of Japan showed • The data is closely watched by the BOJ for clues on the extent to which companies are passing on rising labour costs to service-related prices • The BOJ is set to keep interest rates steady at 1.25 per cent in a two-day meeting concluding on Friday, but signal its readiness to continue raising borrowing costs on mounting price pressures

Source: Reuters
